key_insight: FORA combines recognition of 1,028 radiological concepts, spatial localization and CT report generation in one model trained without manually annotated lesions.
engineering_relevance: For computational imaging and fracture assessment, FORA demonstrates report-supervised localization of findings such as rib fractures, rather than mechanical damage prediction.
method: Train on 304,962 routine CT examinations paired with radiology reports.
Use multiple-instance learning to localize abnormalities without lesion-level supervision.
Connect spatial evidence to findings and report generation through an interpretable concept bottleneck.
evidence_signal: On 36,619 held-out CT examinations, FORA achieved 0.918 macro AUROC for concept recognition; independent localization tests showed lesion-hit rates up to 348 times chance.
watch_item: Clinical deployment requires further validation beyond the represented CT protocols; strong recognition and localization do not by themselves establish report safety.
paper_title: Reliable and grounded reporting of any computed tomography scan with FORA
